is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae (s.l.) vectors, specifically An. gambiae (s.s.) and An. arabiensis (Page 1, Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F (kdr-w) and Ace-1 G280S (Ace-1R) (Page 3, Methods; Page 5, Results).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper provides genotype counts for kdr-w (RR, RS, SS) for the total sample and segregated by species/molecular form (Page 5, Results; Page 6, Fig 4).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from field sites in Kome, southern Chad (Page 2, Methods).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an original empirical study evaluating insecticide resistance in field-collected mosquitoes.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study specifies two sites in Kome, Logone Oriental region, Chad, with coordinates provided (Page 2, Methods).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Sampling took place from 15th October 2013 to 7th November 2013 (Page 2, Methods).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes a new collection of mosquitoes in 2013.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data is included in the main text and figures.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated insecticide resistance in Anopheles gambiae (s.l.) from two sites in Kome, southern Chad, in 2013. It found high phenotypic resistance to pyrethroids, DDT, and carbamates, but susceptibility to organophosphates. Genotyping revealed the presence of the kdr-w (L995F) mutation, particularly in An. coluzzii, while Ace-1R was not detected.
